=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/plan_nothing_to_implement_verify.sh:215-226 (Step 6, `close_failed` branch) | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The label swap (`--remove-label 'ai:blocked' --add-label 'ai:closed'`) runs before `gh issue close`, so if the close fails the script reports `outcome=blocked reason=passed detail=close_failed`, and the blocked handler in .github/workflows/plan.yml:2611-2616 adds `ai:blocked` but never removes `ai:closed`.
  WHY: The open issue keeps both labels, and scripts/orchestrate_lib.py lines 2437-2438 (priority list at line 1517) checks `ai:closed` first and classifies the issue as terminal (`label_ai_closed`), which contradicts the blocked comment and the agents.d/10015 "keeps the block" contract; all five reviewers rated it NIT, and the suggested fix is a best-effort `--remove-label 'ai:closed'` before `pnti_finish ... close_failed`.
- scripts/implement_commit_changes.sh:536-542 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The new `if git add ... else outcome=refused reason=add_failed` branch makes every staging failure of a granted `.github/ai/<file>` non-fatal, not just the ignored-path case the new test covers.
  WHY: Before this change, `git add` aborted the step under `set -e`; now any failure (read error, permissions, index lock) lets the step commit the other staged changes without the granted file (commit path 836-898) and still report `did_commit=true`, which publishes a partial implementation; gemini, minimax and luna rated it MAJOR, glm rated it NIT, so the highest is used.
- scripts/implement_commit_changes.sh:538 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `git add ... >/dev/null 2>&1` throws away the actual git error, so the fixed token `reason=add_failed` cannot tell an intended ignored-path refusal from an index lock, permissions or I/O error.
  WHY: An operator or log parser reading `outcome=refused reason=add_failed` cannot tell whether the omission was expected, so the fail-open path has no trigger anyone can diagnose.
- agents.d/9920-github-ai-plan-grant-write.md:10 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: scripts/implement_commit_changes.sh:541 now emits an optional `reason=add_failed` token on the `refused` outcome, but the `IMPLEMENT_GITHUB_AI_GRANT ... outcome=staged|absent|refused` registry entry does not document it.
  WHY: Nothing fails at runtime, but the emitted log line has drifted from the contractual log-prefix registry that log analysis and the materiality check read.
- agents.d/10015-plan-nothing-to-implement-verify.md:10 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The registry entry `IMPLEMENT_GITHUB_AI_GRANT ... outcome=staged|absent|refused` was not updated to include the new `reason=add_failed` detail.
  WHY: Nothing fails at runtime, but the emitted log line and the contractual registry have drifted apart, which may affect automated auditing.
- scripts/check_failure_triage.sh:823-827 (triage_target_files_guard) | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The new truncation check (`guard_files_total >= 20`) makes the guard fail open and keep the route when the failing-file list is truncated.
  WHY: A truncated list cannot prove that every failing file on the head is also present on the target branch, so a possibly wrong route is kept on incomplete evidence (rated MAJOR).
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
